Bwindi Impenetrable National Park · Southwestern Uganda, Uganda

Bwindi Impenetrable National Park

Bwindi works best for travelers who understand that the reward is not speed or comfort, but the emotional intensity of one hour with a habituated gorilla family after a demanding forest trek.

Photos: Thomas Fuhrmann (CC BY-SA 4.0). Displayed images may be resized or cropped. Photo details.

What it is

Bwindi is an ancient, steep-sided Albertine Rift rainforest and a UNESCO World Heritage landscape. Its signature experience is tracking a habituated mountain-gorilla family from one of four UWA entry sectors: Buhoma, Ruhija, Rushaga, or Nkuringo.

What draws people here

  • One closely managed hour with a habituated mountain-gorilla family
  • Buhoma, Ruhija, Rushaga, and Nkuringo forest sectors
  • Albertine Rift birds and primates

How to get there

Most travelers fly into Entebbe and continue by domestic flight or a long but scenic road transfer into southwestern Uganda. Permit logistics should be secured early and matched to the correct trekking sector.

Best time

Drier months usually make the trails easier, though trekking runs year-round.

Planning notes

A permit is tied to a date and entry sector, so confirm the sector before choosing a lodge.
